project.name: Tempo Robot SW
project.description: ROS2-based autonomous robotic platform running on NVIDIA Jetson hardware with Docker-containerized development environment, Isaac ROS base images, and a modular ROS2 node architecture.

notes: VS Code is typically used inside the docker container via the Dev Container extension.
Commands such as buildsw and startsw must be run inside the container shell.
The `scripts/tempo_startup.sh` script is run on the host at boot using the Ubuntu startup
applications mechanism. It ensures the docker container is running and starts the robot
software inside it. If the docker container exits, it is automatically restarted using the

rules: Always use build_sw instead of `colcon` build for normal development.
Only use `colcon` build directly when explicitly debugging the build system.
buildsw automatically sources all workspaces, sets the correct build configuration, and handles build order and dependencies.

notes: Use tempo_launch host.launch.py as the main entry point.
Use is_sim launch argument to switch between hardware and simulation.

hardware: Arduino or CAN bus motor control

monitoring_telemetry.events: JSON logging for robot state transitions
monitoring_telemetry.metrics: Postgres via files ingested by fluentbit in a host docker service

web_ui.startup: launched by docker compose through dstartweb in tempostartup.sh

core_nodes: tempo_usage_tracking (Shapely-based polygon tracking for grinding usage)

motor_control.protocol: custom CAN messages for motor control
motor_control.rs485: used for main grinder motor control

state_management.enum_usage_rule: Use TempoState enum for robot states in Python code.

general.pattern: Modular ROS2 nodes with clear separation of concerns.
general.state_updates: Use periodic state updates via topics and services to ensure robustness and correct recovery after failures.

allowed_comment_purpose: Group related code sections using organizational comments.
examples_good: Thread-safe callback from ROS spinner thread.
style_rules: Use organizational comments to group related code sections.
Comment complex algorithms or non-obvious logic.
Apply the same principles to docstrings: describe what the code does, not why it changed.

docstring_conventions.first_line: Concise summary ending with a period.

imports.location_rule: All import statements must be at the top of the file only.
workflow: Before adding any import, read lines 1-30 of the target file.
Check existing imports at the top of the file.
Add new imports only in the top-level imports section, before any function or class definitions.

inline_import_cleanup.rule: Inline imports found inside functions are incorrect and must be moved to the top of the file.

imports.assumption: Assume imports build and resolve correctly; do not add speculative imports.

constants.magic_numbers_rule: Use named constants instead of magic numbers and strings.
constants.placement: Define constants at the top of the file.

class_initialization.preference: Initialize values inside the class rather than only in __init__ where applicable.

common_utils.qos_profile: Use DEFAULT_QOS from tempoutils.util for ROS subscribers and publishers.
common_utils.time_functions: Use functions from tempoutils.time for time conversions and arithmetic.
common_utils.math: Use helpers from tempoutils.math where applicable.
common_utils.datetime: Use datetime utilities from tempoutils.datetime_utils and prefer UTC.

time_handling.ros2_time: Use ROS2 time (rclpy/rclcpp clock) inside ROS2 nodes to support simulated time.
time_handling.utc: Use UTC consistently for system times; convert external timezones via tempoutils.datetime_utils.

features: New features and nodes must be configurable via launch file arguments.

formatter_config: Use project-specific C/C++ style from repository config files.

usage: Between classes and structs in .h files.

linting_and_style_configs.python: .flake8 and .isort.cfg in config folder for style guidance.

rule: If code is reused across modules, move it into shared utilities or common files, following existing project structure and conventions.

new_files: Must follow naming and organizational conventions already in the repo.

state_machine.recovery: Design behaviors to allow safe recovery to correct state after restarts or failures.

navigation.nav2_bt_usage: Use Nav2 BT Navigator as backbone.
navigation.behavior_orchestration: Use tempo_orchestrator to interact with the BT Navigator and implement high-level behaviors.
navigation.path_tracking: Use Pure Pursuit for low-level trajectory tracking.
navigation.slam: Use GLIM-based SLAM with Livox Mid360 lidar.

event_logging.content: robot state transitions and key events

metrics.ingestion: files produced by custom classes and ingested by fluentbit in a host docker service

startup_behavior.auto_launch: Web app can auto-launch robot software at startup based on configuration.
startup_behavior.host_integration: Host launches web app via docker compose in tempostartup.sh using dstartweb alias.

integrations: Default GitLab issue and MR workflows as per template.
Optional GitLab CI/CD pipelines, SAST, and deployment options provided by GitLab.

rule_updates.when_corrected: When the user corrects assistant behavior, propose adding a new explicit rule to this configuration to avoid repeating the mistake.
